text:
alex: Need to provision a new GPU node pool in asia-northeast1 for a Japan-facing embed/candidates workload. Low latency, bursty traffic. Any quota landmines?

priya: +1. Are we thinking dedicated A10g or a mixed pool with cheaper T4s for lower-priority jobs?

alex: Ideally mixed. Serving should hit A10g; batch/cold jobs on T4 spot. Want to avoid overprovisioning and long startup times.

kevin: Quick quota check — project quota for GPUs in asia-northeast1 is currently 40 GPUs (per compute quota). We have ~18 used. Can request increase but it can take 48-72h. infra-bot: /quota-check returned: GPUs=40 total, 18 used, 22 available.

maria: If quota increase is slow, we could create a small A10g pool (6-8 GPUs) + a larger T4 spot pool and route pods via nodeSelector/affinity + taints. That buys immediate cap.

alex: Good. Two followups: 1) autoscaler behavior for mixed-instance pools? 2) how to prevent scale-down killing long-running KV-cache warm pods?

priya: For cluster-autoscaler on mixed pools, careful with resource requests — CA picks nodes by unschedulable pods. Use PodPriority and nodeAffinity to prefer A10g for prod. Also set scale-down-utilization-threshold to 0.5 so it doesn't eagerly delete nodes.

kevin: Also consider setting podDisruptionBudget for the warm pods and annotated pods to avoid scale-down. Example PDB: 

```yaml
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: kv-warm-pdb
spec:
  maxUnavailable: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: kv-warm
```

maria: For startup time, use node-local cache init containers and a prewarm DaemonSet on A10g nodes. Taints: add taint gpu:type=A10g:NoSchedule and tolerate on prod pods. T4 pool can be tainted gpu:type=T4:PreferNoSchedule.

alex: What about node-ttl/scale down delays? I want nodes to persist long enough for infrequent bursts.

priya: On GKE use --scale-down-delay-after-add 15m (or higher) and --scale-down-unneeded-time 20m. If using autoscaler v1, set --max-empty-bulk-delete 0 to avoid mass deletion. If Karpenter, set consolidation disabled for those node templates.

kevin: Network egress: asia-northeast1 bandwidth per GPU instance is limited on some SKUs. A10g has higher NIC than T4; watch pod CNI MTU and bursting. We should run a quick iperf test after provisioning.

infra-bot: Deploy ticket created: INFRA-1247. Requested nodepool: asia-northeast1-a10g-prod (6 GPUs), asia-northeast1-t4-spot (12 GPUs). Quota request filed for +20 GPUs. ETA: 72h for quota.

maria: Cost note: A10g on-demand ~ $X/hr, T4 spot ~ $Y/hr. If bursts are frequent, cost could be ~30-40% higher than just reserved A10g. Suggest monitoring by route and enabling per-node label billing tags.

alex: Thanks. Last piece — kube-scheduler preemption/eviction behavior. If A10g pool fills, we should fallback to lower-quality model on T4 or a quantized variant. How do we configure fallback?

priya: Application side: implement runtime routing — check node labels or use topologySpreadConstraint + a priorityClass. Fallback can be implemented via admission webhook that rewrites model image tag to quantized variant when a pod lands on T4. More work but safest.

kevin: Operational checklist for provisioning:
- create node pools with taints and labels
- set CA configs: scale-down-delay, unneeded-time
- add PDBs for warm pods
- enable per-node billing labels
- run iperf and gpu-smoke after create

alex: I'll approve INFRA-1247 once the ticket adds the exact instance SKUs and cost estimate. Anyone want to add sanity checks to the ticket?

maria: Add a preflight job: 
```
kubectl run gpu-smoke --image=nvcr.io/nvidia/cuda:11.8-base --restart=Never --limits='nvidia.com/gpu=1' --rm -- /bin/bash -c "nvidia-smi"
```

priya: Also add a config snippet for CA: 
```yaml
--scale-down-delay-after-add=20m
--scale-down-unneeded-time=25m
--scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.5
```

infra-bot: Note: quota increased to +10 GPUs overnight by cloud provider (pending confirmation). Update in ticket when confirmed.

alex: Great — thanks all. I'll update INFRA-1247 and loop in finance for cost approval. :thumbsup:
